verdict: contracts.js is genuinely at the bar on almost every axis the rubric measures and beats cost.js on breadth: one guarded chokepoint for every .from(/.rpc( in /src/transport (verified — zero query calls in the other six files), both the r.error and the try/catch guard on every DB call, a three-way ok/missing/offline split with a stateless MISSING_RE and a named-dependency branch that fires BEFORE the generic one, an error table that matches sql/038 exactly 35 codes to 35 with an unknown arm that prints the code verbatim, an atomic verify-then-deduct-then-unwind spend with refundRes for undo and addRes for payout and the distinction argued as a safety property, one save() chokepoint that converts false into a throw so the refund branches stay live code, addGems carrying a named reason, and rejected designs (the P2P vehicle market, the client day key, crediting the carrier locally) recorded with their costs. It also does something the brief did not ask for and got right: it read sql/038 on disk, found transport_dispatch declares NINE arguments rather than the brief's five, and sent all nine with the PGRST202 consequence spelled out. The failure is one place, and it is the money path. The dispatch() object-form overload asserts in a comment that index.js:664 hands it 'the whole request'; routes.js's shape() (routes.js:503-528) returns carrierId/hops/escort/cargoUnits and NOT cargo, from, to or rigId, so dispatch(S.quote) falls straight into the bad_cargo arm and no freight can ever be shipped in the assembled app. The file could not have fixed that alone — but it could have read the sibling file it was citing, and instead it claims the drift is absorbed. Secondary: several index.html line citations are ~250 lines stale (inherited from the brief but not verified against the file), and one phrase inside quotation marks is not the quote.
biggest_gap: dispatch()'s object-form overload reads q.cargo / q.from / q.to / q.rigId off routes.js's quote object, which shape() (public/src/transport/routes.js:503-528) does not carry — so index.js:664's dispatch(S.quote) always returns the bad_cargo refusal and the feature's only money path is dead end-to-end, while contracts.js:944-945 states that call site is handled. contracts.js cannot invent the manifest, so the fix is to stop asserting the drift is absorbed: detect the quote-shaped object (ok/code/etaText/cargoUnits present, cargo absent) and return a named refusal that says index.js must pass the request it quoted, not the quote — the same 'name the real error instead of guessing' rule the file applies everywhere else.
